label: PuraYume — 125 BPM house
palette:
# PuraYume — classic 125 BPM house, Roland-flavored synth
# Translated from a Strudel spec (see meta.strudelSource):
#   kick:4 four-on-the-floor · ~snare~snare backbeat · hat offbeats
#   sawtooth melody f3 [g3*2] g#3 d#3 ~ f3 with .lpf(900) .room(0.3)
# Melody uses 'bass' voice: it IS the engine's sawtooth + resonant LPF
# combo (sweeps 220 -> 900 -> 180 Hz), so the gritty Roland-synth feel
# is built in. Reverb is added by 'fx bass reverb 0.3' in the arrangement.
kick:  x ~ ~ ~  x ~ ~ ~  x ~ ~ ~  x ~ ~ ~
snare: ~ ~ ~ ~  x ~ ~ ~  ~ ~ ~ ~  x ~ ~ ~
chh:   ~ ~ x ~  ~ ~ x ~  ~ ~ x ~  ~ ~ x ~
# 1-bar melodic loop at 8th notes: f3, g3, g3 (the [g3*2] double), g#3,
# d#3, rest, f3, rest. The G->G# chromatic move + F->D# fifth interval
# are the defining gestures.
bass:  f3 g3 g3 g#3  d#3 ~ f3 ~  /2
arrangement:
@length 64

0   section intro
0   in kick
4   in chh

12  section groove
12  in snare
16  in bass
16  fx bass reverb 0.3

24  section warm
24  filter 6000 6        ; gentle global LPF close — the underground-warehouse depth

32  section break
32  out kick
32  filter 1100 8        ; deeper close, kickless

40  section return
40  in kick
40  filter 18000 4       ; open the filter back up

48  section roll
48  euclid kick 11 16    ; busier kick variation for the build

56  section riser
56  riser 8
60  filter 18000 4       ; full open into the loop point

meta.title: PuraYume

translationNotes.tempo: 125 BPM, sits in the 120-126 'European club bounce' range called out in the brief.
translationNotes.every(2, inv): Strudel's 'every 2 cycles, invert the kick' adds a 2-bar variation. The studio's pattern grammar has no per-cycle conditional, and a strict inversion of a one-hit-per-cycle kick reads as silence-then-busy rather than 'rolling house'. Dropped in favor of straight 4-on-the-floor + a euclid(11,16) variation in the 'roll' section (bar 48), which gives the same 'kick gets busier' build the inversion gestures at.
translationNotes.hat:1*4 vs offbeats: Strudel's *4 puts hats on quarters (with the kicks). Mapped to offbeats here — that's the 'tssss tssss' between-kick hat that defines house. If you prefer quarters, swap chh's pattern to 'x ~ ~ ~  x ~ ~ ~  x ~ ~ ~  x ~ ~ ~'.
translationNotes.sawtooth + lpf(900): The 'bass' voice is the engine's sawtooth-into-resonant-LPF combo. Its envelope sweeps 220 -> 900 -> 180 Hz with Q=8, so the cutoff sits at the requested 900 Hz at the peak of each note. Plays as a Roland-style filtered saw at the f3/g3/d#3 register.
translationNotes.room(0.3): Realized via 'fx bass reverb 0.3' at bar 16 — bass has no default reverb send so it's explicitly opened. The studio's reverb is a 2.4 s convolver.

meta.voiceCaveats: If a future build adds a brighter 'lead' voice that better matches the Roland-saw timbre, the melody track can be swapped from 'bass' to that voice with no other change.
